full_text.Title: Side-chain-type poly(arylene ether sulfone)s containing multiple quaternary ammonium groups as anion exchange membranes

Sections.name: Introduction
content: Fuel cells are widely regarded as promising clean power sources because of their ability to convert energy stored in fuels directly and efficiently into electrical energy without emission of polluting chemicals . In the past decade, there has been a growing attentions in the development of anion exchange membrane fuel cells (AEMFCs), since they can combine the advantages of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) and traditional alkaline fuel cells . Compared to PEMFCs, AEMFCs exhibited faster electrokinetics under alkaline conditions for oxygen reduction and fuel oxidation reactions at the electrodes. This allows utilization of non-noble metal catalysts as electrode materials, thus reducing the cost significantly. Moreover, the choices of fuels were more flexible, many kinds of fuels (e.g., methanol, ethanol, and ethylene glycol) could be used, because of the low overpotential for hydrocarbon fuel oxidation and reduced fuel crossover.

As a crucial component in AEMFCs, the anion exchange membranes (AEMs) play a dominate role in transporting anions between electrodes and preventing fuels crossover. Because the commercially available AEMs are not as ion conductive and stable as the proton exchange membranes (PEMs), much efforts have been devoted to developing better AEM materials . Aromatic ionomers are the preferred candidates for fuel cell applications due to their good thermal and mechanical properties as well as flexible synthetic route. In the recent literatures, a variety of poly(aryl ether)s were applied to AEMs by introducing quaternized ammonium , imidazolium or guanidinium . These AEMs are typically prepared by chloromethylation on aromatic rings or bromination on the methyl groups of the polymer main chain, followed by the Menshutkin reaction with tertiary amine, pentamethylguanidine, or methylimidazole to form benzylammonium, benzylguanidinium, or benzylimidazolyl groups, respectively.

For fuel cell applications, the successful AEMs must meet certain stringent requirements, including high hydroxide conductivity, low swelling ratio, and good chemical stability. In general, AEMs require high ion exchange capacities (IEC) to attain high water uptake and considerable hydroxide conductivity due to the low mobility of hydroxide ion. However, the high water uptake usually leads to severe swelling, or even a disintegration of the AEMs at elevated temperature . This trade-off between ion conductivity and dimensional stability is still a crucial issue that requires improvement through careful structural design. In the pursuit of hydrocarbon-based aromatic PEMs with improved properties, it has been demonstrated that locating the hydrophilic ionic groups on side chains of the polymer main chain is one promising approach to enhance the stability and conductivity of aromatic ionomer [35]. In our previous work, we reported a series of side-chain-type poly(arylene ether sulfone)s containing densely populated sulfonic acid pendant units by post-sulfonation . These sulfonated polymers displayed advantageous proton conductivities with relatively low water contents and good conductivity-swelling behavior. The strategy of utilizing a “side-chain-type” structure is also expected to be useful in AEMs . However, few aromtic ionomers containing anion conducting groups on the polymer side chains have been synthesized due to the lack of appropriate monomers and convent approches that can efficiently introduce anion-conductive groups onto the polymer side chains.

In the present work, a new reactive difluorodiphenyl sulfone monomer with four pendent 3,5-dimethylphenyl groups were synthesized by a two-step reaction. A series of side-chain-type poly(arylene ether sulfone)s containing eight pendant quaternary ammonium groups in side chains were prepared as anion exchange membranes by polycondensation of this monomer with DFDPS and BP, followed by reactions of bromination and quaternization. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported example of side-chain-type AEMs containing multiple pendant quaternary ammonium groups in each repeated unit. The structures of the monomer and the resulting membranes are characterized in detail, and some elected properties of the membranes are also investigated and discussed.

content.name: Materials
content: 4,4′-Difluorodiphenyl sulfone (DFDPS), 3,5-dimethylbenzeneboronic acid, 4,4′-biphenol (BP), N-bromosuccinimide (NBS), benzoyl peroxide (BPO), and tetrakis(triphenylphosphine) palladium (0) were purchased from TCI Company and used as received. Commercially available N-methyl-2-pyrrolidinone (NMP), toluene, 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and other reagents were all used as received.

content.name: Synthesis of 3,3′,5,5′-Tetrabromo-4,4′-difluorodiphenyl sulfone (TB-DFDPS)
content: 3,3′,5,5′-Tetrabromo-4,4′-difluorodiphenyl sulfone (mp: 180–182 °C) was synthesized according to the method reported in our preceding studies .

content.name: Synthesis of 3,3′,5,5′-tetra(3′′,5′′-dimethylphenyl)-4,4′-difluorodiphenyl sulfone (M-DFDPS)
content: To a 1 L three-necked round-bottom flask equipped with a reflux condenser, mechanical stirrer and nitrogen inlet, 11.40 g (0.02 mol) TB-DFDPS, 12.60 g (0.084 mol) 3,5-dimethylbenzeneboronic acid, 16.96 g (0.16 mol) sodium carbonate, 2.00 g (0.0017 mol) tetrakis(triphenylphosphine) palladium(0), 200 mL toluene, 50 mL 1,2-dimethoxyethane and 200 mL water were added. The reaction mixture was heated at 100 °C with vigorous stirring. After about 10 h, some solvents were evaporated from the mixture to obtain a suspension solution. The precipitate was collected and the crude solid was recrystallized from N,N-dimethylacetamide to yield 10.06 g of white crystals. Yield: 75%, mp: 253–254 °C. ^{1}H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl_{3}; ppm): 7.99 (d, J=6.0, 4H, H_{a}), 7.17 (s, 8H, H_{b}), 7.06 (s, 4H, H_{c}), 2.38 (s, 24H, –CH_{3}). ^{13}C NMR (100 MHz, CDCl_{3}; ppm): 159.27 (d, J=206.6, C_{4}), 138.16 (C_{7}), 137.36 (C_{1}), 133.85 (C_{5}), 131.48 (C_{3}), 130.15 (C_{8}), 129.09 (C_{2}), 126.82 (C_{6}), 21.18 (–CH_{3}).

content.name: Synthesis of poly(arylene ether sulfone)s containing pendant metheyl groups (PAES-M-xx)
content: A typical synthetic procedure, illustrated by the preparation of PAES-M-16 copolymer (xx=16: M-DFDPS/DFDPS=16/84), is described as follows. To a 50 mL round-bottomed flask equipped with a Dean-Stark trap, condenser, a mechanical stirrer and nitrogen inlet. 0.5367 g (0.8 mmol) M-DFDPS, 1.0679 g (4.2mmol) DFDPS, 0.9311 g (5 mmol) BP, 0.8280 g (6 mmol) K_{2}CO_{3}, 9 mL NMP and 3 mL toluene were added The reaction mixture was refluxed at 140 °C for 4 h to remove water. After removal of toluene and water, the reaction temperature was raised to 170 °C. After 5–8 h, 3 mL of NMP was added to the mixture to reduce the solution viscosity. The solution was poured into 500 mL deionized water with vigorous stirring. The resulting fibrous copolymer was washed several times with deionized water and dried at 100 °C under vacuum for 6 h.

content.name: Synthesis of bromomethylated poly(arylene ether sulfone)s (PAES-Br-xx)
content: A typical procedure for the preparation of PAES-Br-16 was as follows. To a 100 mL three-necked flask equipped with mechanical stirrer, nitrogen inlet and condenser, 1.0 g PAES-M-16 and 40 mL 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane were added. The mixture was stirred adequately to form homogeneous solution. Then 0.98 g NBS and 0.07 g BPO were added and the solution was heated to 80 °C. After 4 h, the dark-orange solution was poured into ethanol and the precipitated polymer was subsequently washed repeatedly in hot water. The resulting polymer was dried under vacuum at 100 °C for 6 h.

content.name: Synthesis of quaternary-aminated poly(arylene ether sulfone)s (PAES-Q-xx)
content: A typical procedure for the preparation of PAES-Q-16 was as follows. To a 100 mL three-necked flask equipped with mechanical stirrer, 0.8 g PAES-Br-16 and 16 mL N-methylpyrrolidone were added. The mixture was stirred adequately to form homogeneous solution. Then 2 mL of 33% trimethylamine aqueous solution was added and the mixture was stirred at room temperature. After 48 h, the solution was precipitated in IPA, washed and dried at 60 °C under vacuum.

content.name: Membrane preparation and characterizaiton
content: The quaternary-aminated copolymers (0.6 g) were readily dissolved in 10 mL of DMSO firstly. The solution was filtrated and cast onto a leveled glass plate, and dried at 80 °C for 24 h. Then, the membranes were removed from the glass by immersion in water and further kept in a 1.0 M NaOH solution for 48 h. Finally, the membranes were washed thoroughly and immersed in deionized water for 48 h to remove the residual NaOH before use.

NMR spectra were measured on a 400 MHz Bruker AV 300 spectrometer using CDCl_{3} and DMSO-d 6 as solvent. Gel permeation chromatography (GPC) on soluble polymers was performed on a Waters 515 system using tetrahydrofuran (THF) as the eluent. Ion exchange capacities (IEC) of the membranes were determined by titration. A sample membrane in the OH^{−} form was immersed in 20 mL of 0.1 M HCl standard for 48 h. The solutions were then titrated with a standardized NaOH solution using phenolphthalein as an indicator. The thermogravimetric analyses (TGA) were obtained in nitrogen with a Perkin-Elmer TGA-2 thermogravimetric analyzer at a heating rate of 10 °C/min. The chemical stability was evaluated by immersing the PAES-Q-xx membranes into a 4 M NaOH solution at room temperature for a certain time. After being shaken lightly, the shape of the test sample was observed. The alkaline stability was determined from changes of the IEC value and conductivity of the membranes.

The hydroxide conductivity (σ, mS/cm) of each membrane coupon (size: 1 cm×4 cm) was obtained using σ=d/L _{s} W _{s} R (d: distance between reference electrodes, and L _{s} and W _{s} are the thickness and width of the membrane, respectively). The resistance value (R) was measured over the frequency range from 100 mHz to 100 kHz by four-point probe alternating current (ac) impedance spectroscopy using an electrode system connected with an impedance/gain-phase analyzer (Solartron 1260) and an electrochemical interface (Solartron 1287, Farnborough, Hampshire, UK). The membranes were sandwiched between two pairs of gold-plate electrodes. The membranes and the electrodes were set in a Teflon cell and the distance between the reference electrodes was 1.0 cm. Conductivity measurements under fully hydrated conditions were carried out in a thermo-controlled chamber with the cell immersed in liquid water.

The water uptake and swelling ratio were determined by measuring the difference in weight and length between dry and hydrated membranes.Water uptake of the membranes was calculated from Eq. content.name: Synthesis of monomer
content: A new difluorodiphenyl sulfone monomer containing four pendent 3,5-dimethylphenyl groups was synthesized by a two-step reaction as shown in Scheme 1. Firstly, the precursor TB-DFDPS was synthesized by bromination of 4,4′-difluorodiphenyl sulfone using NBS. The reaction was conducted in concentrated sulfuric acid as solvent and catalyst, as reported in our preceding studies . Following this, 3,3′,5,5′-tetra(3′′,5′′-dimethylphenyl)-4,4′-difluorodiphenyl sulfone (M-DFDPS) was produced by Suzuki coupling reaction of TB-DFDPS with 3,5-dimethylbenzeneboronic acid. Multiple benzylmethyl groups in this monomer were designed as side chain sites for quaternary ammonium functionalization. The structure of M-DFDPS was confirmed by NMR spectroscopy. Fig. 1a and b were the ^{1}H NMR and ^{13}C NMR spectra of M-DFDPS, respectively. As shown in Fig. 1a, the assignments of each proton were given and the protons of methyl groups appared at 2.38 ppm. In the ^{13}C NMR spectrum, the carbon of methyl groups appeard at 21.18 ppm and all aromatic carbons appeard at 125–165 ppm. According to Fig. 1b, C_{4} showed clear doublets because of the C–F coupling (coupling constant J _{C–F}=206.6 Hz). The chemical shifts for all carbons in M-DFDPS were assigned with the aid of the 2D COSY spectra. All these spectra agreed well with the proposed molecular structure, which indicated the successful preparation of the target monomer.

content.name: Synthesis of copolymers
content: A series of poly(arylene ether sulfone) copolymers containing four pendent 3,5-dimethylphenyl groups (PAES-M-xx, xx: mole ratio (%) of M-DFDPS) were prepared via a standard K_{2}CO_{3}-catalyzed aromatic nucleophilic substitution polycondensation using various feed ratios of M-DFDPS/DFDPS as shown in Scheme 2. All the polymerizations proceeded smoothly and afforded homogeneous solutions, indicating that the polymers possessed good solubility in the polymerization medium. The successful copolymerizations were confirmed by ^{1}H NMR spectrum, which showed a characteristic signal at 2.23 ppm arising from methyl groups ( Fig. 2a). The feed ratios for monomers, inherent viscosities and molecular weight results of PAES-M-xx were also given in Table 1. Their inherent viscosities were in the range 0.62–0.71 dL/g in NMP solution, and the number molecular weight (M _{n}) and the weight molecular weight (M _{w}) were in the range 65,000–84,000 and 98,000–134,000, respectively, indicating the formation of medium to reasonably high molecular weight polymers.

Subsequent bromination of PAES-M-xx copolymers was conducted successfully at the benzylmethyl positions using an excess of NBS and BPO as the bromine and radical source, respectively (Scheme 2). This reaction offers an efficient and convenient pathway to introduce positively charged groups exclusively at benzylic positions in aromatic polymers . The high conversion of the benzylic groups was confirmed by the disappearance of the ^{1}H NMR signal at 2.23 ppm and the concurrent appearance of a new signal at 4.40 ppm originating from the benzyl bromide protons (Fig. 2b). After bromination, the introduction of the cationic groups in the copolymers was carried out by substitution of the bromine atoms via reaction with trimethylamine at room temperature. The resultant quaternized copolymers were no longer soluble in chloroform, and hence NMR analysis was performed with DMSO-d _{6} solutions (Fig. 2c). The spectrum of the PAES-Q-16 showed broader and less distinct signals than the PAES-M-16 and PAES-Br-16 materials. Quaternization of the copolymers was indicated by the appearance of a signal at around 2.84–3.16 ppm attributed to the protons of the –N(CH_{3})_{3} groups. The IEC values of the PAES-Q-xx could be readily adjusted by changing the feed ratios of the M-DFDPS and DFDPS, and their measured values were in the range of 1.65–2.36 mequiv/g as shown in Table 2. The quaternized copolymers with higher IEC values were not be proposed due to their poor solubility for casting.

content.name: Water uptake and swelling ratio
content: Water uptake is an important factor for fuel cell membranes and hydroxide transport could be accelerated by the water molecules in AEMs. However, water swelling ratio should be also considered because unrestrained swelling decreases the dimensional stability and mechanical properties of the polymer membranes. In the fields of the membrane preparation, one of the trends is to synthesize low swelling materials even at high IEC levels. The water uptake and swelling ratio of the PAES-Q-xx membranes were evaluated and the results are shown in Table 2 and Fig. 3. As expected, their values both increased with the IEC values and temperature. The present side-chain-type AEMs showed much lower water uptake and swelling ratio than many main-chain-type AEMs at equal IEC values . Using the PAES-Q-20 membrane (IEC=2.36 mequiv/g) as an example, the water uptake and swelling ratio were just 22.5% and 6.7% at 20° C, respectively. As for the main-chain-type AEM with IEC value of 2.29 mequiv/g [25], the water uptake and swelling ratio were 47% and 23% at 20° C, respectively. The results indicated that PAES-Q-xx membranes possessed better dimentional stability. PAES-Q-xx membranes having densely side-chain-type quaternary ammonium groups may be more effective in separating hydrophilic ionic groups from the hydrophobic polymer main chain. Thus, water molecules can be restricted to hydrophilic domains in the membranes and separated from hydrophobic domains, leading to a suppression of the water swelling. Lower water uptake and swelling also suggested these membranes more competitive for their further applications.

content.name: Hydroxide conductivity
content: The hydroxide conductivity is a particularly important property of ion exchange membranes for fuel cell applications. Generally, the conductivity above 10 mS/cm is required for AEM materials in fuel cells. Before hydroxide conductivity measurements, all membranes were initially hydrated by immersion in deionized water for 24 h at room temperature and then reached a fully hydrated condition. The conductivities of membranes at 20 and 80 °C were reported at Table 2. Similar to the water uptake, the hydroxide conductivity also increased with increasing IEC values and temperature. From Table 2, it could be seen that all the obtained membranes showed conductivities above 10 mS/cm at 20 °C and their conductivities were in the range of 23–37 and 54–82 mS/cm at 20 and 80 °C, respectively. The good conductivity of PAES-Q-xx membranes is probably due to the high IEC values and the dense distribution of the quaternary ammonium groups. Inorder to explore the relationship between water uptake and hydroxide conductivity, Fig. 4 shows the hydroxide conductivity as a function of hydration number (λ), which is the numbe of water molecules per quaternary ammonium group. For comparison, the properties of a representative main-chain-type AEM with two quaternary ammonium groups in each unit (QNPS-OH-60, IEC=2.29 mequiv/g) are also shown in Fig. 4 [25]. It should be noted that high relative water uptake and dimensional swelling can lead to difficulties in MEA fabrication, membrane-electrode interfacial resistance, and membrane creep and deformation. As shown in Fig. 4, an important finding of the present work is that PAES-Q-xx membranes located on the left portion of the graph have comparable hydroxide conductivity but lower water absorption (λ) values compared with that of main-chain-type AEM. These results suggest that the present polymer designed by incorporation of multiple side-chain-type structures is effective for the AEMs in mitigating dimensional swelling and improving hydroxide conductivity, as already demonstrated for acid based PEMs . Because of the densely side-chain quaternary ammonium groups for OH^{−} transport, it is believed that PAES-Q-xx membranes are able to utilize water molecules more efficiently for ion transport.

content.name: Thermal and alkaline stabilities
content: Good thermal properties for AEMs are the necessary requirements for their effective use in fuel cell applications because work at elevated temperatures could enhance the reaction kinetics and reduce the thermodynamic voltage losses. The thermal properties of PAES-Q-xx membranes were measured by TGA at a heating rate of 10 °C/min under a nitrogen atmosphere and the 5% weight loss temperature (T _{d5}) was listed in Table 2. The TGA traces for PEAS-Q-xx and PEAS-M-16 are all presented in Fig. 5. A two-step degradation profile was observed for PAES-Q-xx in their hydroxide form. There was no weight loss up to 200 °C because the samples were preheated at 120 °C for 20 min to remove absorbed water. As shown in figure, the first weight loss occurred at about 220–270 °C, which was associated with the degradation of the quaternary ammonium groups. The second weight loss at around 400–500 °C was related to the degradation of the polymer chain. The decomposition temperature of the polymer backbone was similar to that of the parent polymer PEAS-M-16, suggesting that the decomposition of the quaternary ammonium groups did not trigger degradation of the polymer backbone, which was observed in some aromatic AEMs [40]. Furthermore, It can be seen from Table 2 that the 5% weight loss temperature of these copolymers had a light decrease with increasing IEC values, which further demonstrated that the first weight-loss was caused by degradation of the quaternary ammonium groups.

One of the key requirements for AEMs is good alkaline stability under fuel cell operating conditions. The alkaline stability of PAES-Q-xx membranes was evaluated by immersing the membranes in 4 M NaOH solution at room temperature, and the results are shown in Table 3. In basic conditions, there were two kinds degradation of the AEMs, the degradation of charge groups and the polymer backbone. The degradation of charge groups would reduce the AEMs׳ conductivity, and the degradation of polymer backbone would cause fragment of the AEMs. As shown in Table 3, all these membranes could maintained their shape and flexibility during the testing time (more than 60 days). Their IEC values and hydroxide conductivity also do not have obvious change after the alkaline stability test. These results directly indicated that PAES-Q-xx membranes had good tolerance of a strong alkaline condition and could be used in alkaline fuel cell applications.

Sections.name: Conclusions
content: In conclusion, a new difluorodiphenyl sulfone monomer with four pendent 3,5-dimethylphenyl groups was successfully synthesized by a two-step reaction. Side-chain-type poly(arylene ether sulfone)s containing multiple quaternary ammonium groups in pendant phenyl rings (PAES-Q-xx) were obtained by sequential polycondensation, bromination and quaternization. These ionomers had good membrane-forming properties using DMSO as solvent. The resulting membranes displayed much lower water uptake and swelling ratio compared with some main-chain-type AEMs. PAES-Q-xx membranes also had good hydroxide conductivity and the highest conductivity was 82 mS/cm at 80 °C. The dense distribution of the side-chain-type quaternary ammonium groups and high IEC values are responsible for their good conductivity. In addition, PAES-Q-xx membranes were stable in 4 M NaOH aqueous solutions for 60 days at room temperature. It has been demonstrated that the performance of the AEMs could be improved by designing the structure of polymers. Thus, this work provides a potential strategy for preparing the AEMs with high performance.

full_text.Abstract: A new difluorodiphenyl sulfone monomer, 3,3′,5,5′-tetra(3′′,5′′- dimethylphenyl)-4,4′-difluorodiphenyl sulfone (M-DFDPS), was synthesized and further polymerized to form a series of poly(arylene ether sulfone)s containing four pendent 3,5-dimethylphenyl groups. After bromination of benzylmethyl groups, side-chain-type poly(arylene ether sulfone)s containing multiple quaternary ammonium groups in pendant phenyl rings (PAES-Q-xx) were prepared by quaternization. Their chemical structures and some properties, including water uptake, swelling ratio, hydroxide conductivities, and thermal and alkaline stabilities, were investigated. These PAES-Q-xx membranes with IEC values of 1.65–2.36 mequiv/g had low water uptake and swelling ratio. Their conductivities were all above 10 mS/cm and the values were in the range of 23–37 and 54–82 mS/cm at 20 and 80 °C, respectively. The good conductivity is probably due to the high IEC and the dense distribution of the pendant quaternary ammonium groups. In addition, PAES-Q-xx membranes also displayed good thermal and alkaline stabilities.
